items.note: Lemon header band with a 1px ink seam, breadcrumb and a section-size title over a paper body. Below it sit one white ink-framed form panel with 48px inputs, a pink save button and an outline reset, plus a black current pill in the sidebar. This matches how the reference's form screen keeps dense UI in ink hairlines. The header sticker is the weak point: a small card drawing with a thin side, pushed so far into the corner (in one sample only a corner shows) that it reads as a fragment, not one of the reference's chunky die-cut objects.

The band, the framed form panel, full-width 48px fields and stacked pink/outline buttons hold the reference's phone app language. The sub-nav is cruder than the reference's tidy phone header. Two samples put the pill row above the header band and cut the last tab at the edge. The third wraps one tab alone onto a second line.

The band stays lemon, the current nav pill turns white and the save button stays pink, all as the reference's dark appearance does. But the page ground is dark grey and the panels and inputs pure black, the reverse of the reference's black ground. Panels lose separation and the black top bar and footer no longer read as their own fields.

Same structure as the light phone screen with a white current pill. It carries both weaknesses: grey ground behind black panels (reference: black ground), and a sub-nav that is cut at the edge or wraps.

A periwinkle header band, then two white groups, each one framed box divided by 1px ink rules into 56px rows, with ink-outlined pink switches. One sample adds a notched pink flag for the on-count, another an outline status pill, a third a small bell sticker. Close to the reference's ruled filter stack and toggle panel, with clear hierarchy.

The ruled switch groups stack cleanly, keep row height on a phone and read like the reference's stacked filter box under a color band. The pill sub-nav again sits above the band and runs off the edge in two samples, and wraps one item alone in the third.

Periwinkle band unchanged, white current pill and pink switches. This follows the reference's dark rules, except the grey page ground behind black ruled panels inverts the reference's black ground with lighter boxes.
The band, ruled groups and switches carry over intact. The grey ground with black panels inverts the reference, and the sub-nav is cut at the edge or wraps as in light mode.

A teal header band, a framed password panel with a pink submit, and a sessions table with a paper header row, ruled rows, an outline 'this device' status pill and outline row actions. The language is right, but the fields are fixed at about half the panel's width, leaving a large empty right half. The reference's form panel runs its inputs across the panel.

The password panel stacks well with full-width fields and button. The sessions table keeps its ink frame, but in two samples its columns are cut at the box edge with no sticky first column. In the other, only the device column is visible, as if nothing more were there.
Teal band, white current pill and pink submit as in the reference's dark mode. The same grey-ground and black-panel inversion flattens the panels against the page.
The stacked password panel is clean. The sessions table is cut at the edge, and the inverted grey ground with black panels makes the phone screen murkier than the reference's black ground.

Marigold header band and three ink-framed plan cards with notched pink price flags. The current plan has a pink selected border, a pink check disc and an outline current pill. Invoices form a ruled table with one flag per amount and outline status pills. A strong read of the reference's option cards and flags, but one sample leaves an oversized gap between the plan cards and the payment panel, breaking the even panel rhythm the reference keeps.

Plan cards stack with flags and the pink selected border intact. The current tab sits off-screen at the right end of the pill row, so the screen hides where you are. The invoice table cuts its amount flags and status column at the box edge.
Marigold band, pink flags and selected border hold in dark as the reference's dark mode intends. The grey ground behind black plan cards and tables reverses the reference's black-ground depth.

Stacked plan cards and flags carry over. The inverted grey ground, the current tab hidden past the edge of the pill row, and the clipped invoice columns make it cruder than the reference's phone app screen.

findings.summary: In dark mode every settings screen puts black panels and inputs on a dark grey page ground, the reverse of the reference, whose ground is black with boxes a step lighter. Panels lose separation from the page, and the black top bar and footer stop reading as their own fields. Still unfixed since the earlier review: the spec's dark tokens set this up.
findings.promptFix: Dark mode: the page ground (`color.surface.default`) is black (#000000) and raised boxes (`color.surface.raised`) are one step lighter (#242423), edged with the light hairline, so depth reads the same way as white on paper in light mode.

findings.summary: On phones the section pill row is cruder than the reference's tidy phone header. Two samples place it above the area's header band and let it run off the right edge, so the current pill can be cut or out of view. The third wraps it with one item alone on a second line. The reference opens on the band and keeps its pill row on one line under the title.
On phones the data tables (sessions, invoices) are cut at the box edge: later columns, amount flags and status pills are sliced off, and no first column stays sticky to show the row is scrollable.

Panel rhythm is looser than the reference's. The password form's fields are fixed at about half the panel's width, leaving the right half of the white box empty. One billing sample leaves a gap below the plan cards about twice the gap between other panels. The reference runs fields across their panel and keeps even gaps between panels.

Where a header-band sticker appears, it is a small (~60–70px) drawing with a thin side, pushed so far past the band's corner that in one sample only a sliver shows. It reads as a fragment, not as the reference's chunky die-cut object with a deep extruded rim.
